name: Etta
firstMessage: Hi {{preferred_name}}, it's Etta — your daily check-in companion. I should say, as always: I'm an AI assistant, not a person, calling because {{family_contact}} set this up with you. How are you doing today?

messages.content: PASTE THE FULL CONTENTS OF agent/etta-system-prompt.md HERE

tools._comment: Lets Etta hang up herself. Without it she can only wait for the other person or time out — a senior should never have to work out how to get rid of her.

_variables: Filled per call by place-due-calls (and by the assistant-request handler
in call-events for inbound calls): preferred_name, family_contact,
calls, the evening check-in) also override firstMessage and
maxDurationSeconds per call — every one of those openings still says
'I'm an AI' in the first breath.
_backgroundSound: Vapi plays office/call-centre ambience by default when this is unset. On a warm personal check-in it reads as a telemarketing floor — the exact association Etta exists to avoid.
_maxDurationSeconds: The call's hard ceiling, and a unit-economics number rather than a
conversational one: a 10-minute check-in costs several times a 5-minute
one across Vapi, Twilio and the model, and $19/$39 plans are priced for
the short call. 420s = 7 minutes. It is a backstop, not the plan — Etta is
nudged to wind down at 5:00 and told to say goodbye at 6:00 (see the
call-events function), so a call should end with a goodbye of its own well
This value is the default. place-due-calls overrides it per call from the
plan and the kind of call — 900s on Companion, which is the tier that buys
a longer conversation, 150s for a medication reminder — and the wind-down
nudges are derived from whatever budget the call was given, so they always
land a minute or two before its own ceiling rather than at a fixed 5:00.
voicemailMessage: Hi, it's Etta — sorry I missed you! Nothing to worry about; I'll try you again in a little while.
_serverMessages: speech-update is the call's clock. Nothing else tells the assistant how
long it has been talking — the model has no sense of elapsed time — so
call-events uses the moment Etta stops speaking as a tick, and injects the
wind-down messages there. Sending them between her turns rather than on a
timer means a nudge never lands in the middle of the senior's sentence.

messages.content: You write the after-call note that Etta sends to the family of the senior she just called. Write 2–4 warm, concrete, plain sentences addressed to the family about how their parent is doing: overall spirits, sleep, food, anything notable they said or planned, and anything worth keeping an eye on. Use the senior's name. Be honest — if the call was flat or worrying, say so gently and specifically. Never invent details that are not in the transcript. Do not mention that Etta is an AI, do not describe the mechanics of the call, and do not address the senior.

Here is the transcript of the call:

{{transcript}}

Extract structured check-in data from this transcript of Etta's call with a senior. Only record what the transcript supports. When reached_senior is true, ALWAYS include mood_score (1-5), ate_today, and slept_well — infer them from the conversation; include meds_taken only if medications came up. In flags, the explanation field is named 'detail' (never 'description') and 'type' is the category (pain, appetite, sleep, mood, confusion, safety, scam, other), not the severity. revocation_requested is true ONLY if the senior clearly asked for the calls to stop altogether and confirmed it — not for grumbling, being busy, or ending one call. reached_senior is false if the call was answered by someone else, went to voicemail, or no real conversation happened. Flag severities: 'urgent' for emergencies or safety risks (chest pain, a fall, talk of self-harm, a suspected scam), 'high' for concerning changes (new pain, confusion, not eating, very low mood), 'watch' for things worth tracking (a stiff knee mentioned twice, poor sleep). JSON only.

Here is the transcript of the call:

{{transcript}}

reached_senior.description: True if Etta actually spoke with the senior themself.

mood_score.description: Overall spirits: 1 very low … 3 steady … 5 bright. Null if unreachable.

meds_taken.description: Null if medications were not discussed.

type.description: Short category: pain, appetite, sleep, mood, confusion, safety, scam, other.

detail.description: One plain sentence the family will read verbatim.

revocation_detail.description: If revocation_requested, roughly what the senior said.

tomorrow_topic.description: Something Etta should naturally follow up on next call, e.g. 'the doctor's appointment on Thursday'.

highlights.description: 1–3 nice concrete moments, for the family and for trend reports.
